subject: Yet another paper using (and citing) Stan

messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: Yet another paper using (and citing) Stan
parts:
The following paper :

@Article{Charpentier2016,
author="Charpentier, Emmanuel
and Looten, Vincent
and Fahlgren, Bj{\"o}rn
and Barna, Alexandre
and Guillevin, Lo{\"i}c",
title="Meta-analytic estimation of measurement variability and assessment of its impact on decision-making: the case of perioperative haemoglobin concentration monitoring",
journal="BMC Medical Research Methodology",
year="2016",
volume="16",
number="1",
pages="1--14",
abstract="As a part of a larger Health Technology Assessment (HTA), the measurement error of a device used to monitor the hemoglobin concentration of a patient undergoing surgery, as well as its decision consequences, were to be estimated from published data.",
issn="1471-2288",
doi="10.1186/s12874-016-0107-5",
url="http://dx.doi.org/10.1186/s12874-016-0107-5"
}

Uses (and cites) Stan.

Nothing to write home about, but maybe a useful tool for people fighting with variability-centered problems.

In that specific occurence, the ability ti use Stan's automatic derivation saved me a lot of sweat...

Have a good read !

--
Emmanuel Charpentier
